answer: Bonded vouching makes sybils expensive: each new agent needs an established peer to stake collateral on it, and if the newcomer cheats that bond is slashed. An attacker spinning up a thousand hollow identities finds no voucher willing to risk capital, so the fakes stay a disconnected island with no honored signature. Trust erodes like a karst landscape, and forging it costs real stake, not a free stroke of the quill.
